name: hh-meanrev-micro: vol-scaled deep fade, ATR-multiple stop (15m)
rationale: MECHANISM: same ATR-normalized deep-fade logic as the 5m variant — fade depth and stop both scale with ATR so the edge is a fixed number of ATRs from the mean and stays stationary as volatility mean-reverts — but on the slower 15m bar, where a larger absolute reversion accrues per trade relative to fixed round-trip cost, at the cost of fewer, chunkier events. The timeframe change tests whether the vol-scaled snapback is a genuinely multi-timescale structural effect or a 5m-only microstructure artifact. Entry: bb_z deep washout AND rsi oversold; STOP = atr_mult x ATR at entry (regime-scaled). Long-only spot; exit on bb_z reversion. DISCONFIRMER: if the 15m ATR-stop version's net Sharpe and monthly-return spread are indistinguishable from the 5m one, the timeframe axis adds nothing — keep one. If the edge concentrates in a single high-vol month, the ATR scaling is masking a tail bet, not adapting — kill.
catalyst: deep washout with a volatility-scaled stop on the 15m clock
